result.note: Tests the April 2026 India–South Korea summit outcomes (trade target, CEPA upgrade, new ministerial committee) and the location of the POSCO–JSW steel joint venture.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–South Korea summit held in April 2026:
items: The two sides pledged to double bilateral trade to USD 54 billion by 2030.
They agreed to fast-track talks to upgrade the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, a trade pact dating from 2010.
They established a ministerial-level economic cooperation committee for the first time.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are stated in the story. Prime Minister Modi and President Lee Jae Myung announced the trade target alongside a 250+ person business delegation, and India hopes the CEPA upgrade will narrow its trade deficit while Seoul seeks deeper market access.
questions.source: On Monday, Indian Prime Minister Modi and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung pledged to double bilateral trade to USD 54 billion by 2030, anchored by a 250+ person business delegation and an upgrade of their 2010 trade pact.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, South Korea's POSCO and India's JSW finalised a USD 1.09 billion joint venture for a steel plant in which Indian state?
questions.explain: The POSCO–JSW joint venture is for a steel plant in Odisha. It was finalised during the India–South Korea summit, where 20 other MOUs covering shipbuilding, semiconductors and green energy were also signed.
questions.source: South Korea’s POSCO and India’s JSW finalised a USD 1.09 billion joint venture for a steel plant in Odisha.
